description: Managing real software projects at graduate depth: tailoring a process, estimating under uncertainty, quantifying risk, measuring with care, shipping continuously and leading distributed teams. Students plan and re-plan projects in the diagram studio, run Monte Carlo schedule and risk analyses, and make management decisions in branching case studies.
modelledOn: Boehm and Turner, Balancing Agility and Discipline
outcomes: Select and tailor a software process to a project's size, risk, regulation and team context, and defend the choice.
Produce estimates with ranges using parametric, analogy-based and simulation methods, and plan releases from them.
Run qualitative and quantitative risk analysis and use decision analysis to choose among responses.
Choose goal-driven metrics, compute earned-value and flow measures, and recognise how metrics are gamed.
Design a continuous delivery pipeline and release strategy that balances speed with safety.
Lead distributed and cross-functional teams, assess process maturity and plan a measured improvement programme.

units.title: Process models and tailoring
topics: Plan-driven, iterative, agile and flow-based models compared: waterfall, spiral, unified process, Scrum, extreme programming, Kanban
Tailoring factors: size, criticality, volatility, culture and team experience
Balancing agility and discipline; the home-ground analysis
Processes for regulated and safety-critical domains, and for health and fintech products
Value-stream mapping and finding waste in a process

units.title: Estimation and planning under uncertainty
topics: Why estimates fail: the cone of uncertainty, optimism and anchoring
Parametric models: COCOMO II and function points
Expert and relative estimation: Delphi, planning poker, reference-class forecasting
Critical path, PERT and critical chain scheduling
Monte Carlo schedule simulation and confidence-level commitments
Release and sprint planning; velocity and throughput forecasting
Budgeting and resource levelling for multiple projects

units.title: Risk and decision management
topics: Risk identification: checklists, assumption analysis and pre-mortems
Qualitative analysis: probability-impact matrices and risk exposure
Quantitative analysis: expected monetary value, decision trees and Monte Carlo simulation
Risk response and contingency reserves; supplier and security risk
Decision records, trade-off analysis and cost of delay

units.title: Metrics-driven management
topics: Goal-question-metric and the validity of measurement
Product and quality metrics: defect density, escaped defects, complexity and technical debt
Flow metrics: lead time, cycle time, work in progress, flow efficiency and cumulative flow
Delivery performance measures: deployment frequency, change failure rate and recovery time
Earned value management: planned and earned value, cost and schedule indices, estimate at completion
Control charts, dashboards, Goodhart's law and gaming of metrics

units.title: Continuous delivery and release engineering
topics: Continuous integration and delivery pipelines; trunk-based development and branching strategies
Release strategies: blue-green, canary, dark launches and feature flags
Infrastructure as code, environments and configuration management
Versioning, change control and release trains; mobile releases in low-bandwidth markets
Site reliability: service-level objectives, error budgets and on-call
Incident management and blameless post-incident review

units.title: Distributed and cross-functional teams
topics: Conway's law, team topologies and architecture-aligned teams
Working across time zones: communication, documentation and remote rituals
Outsourcing and vendor contracts; open-source collaboration and governance
Team development, psychological safety and handling conflict
Building engineering teams in African tech hubs: hiring, retention and mentoring
Leading technical staff: delegation, code review culture and performance conversations

units.title: Scaling, governance and failure
topics: Scaling agile: SAFe, LeSS and Nexus compared; portfolio planning
Business case, benefit realisation and product management with OKRs
Contracting: fixed price, time and materials, and outcome-based; public-sector procurement
Case studies of large project failure: causes and warning signs
Project recovery: resetting scope, replanning and rebuilding trust

units.title: Process assessment and improvement
topics: CMMI maturity and capability levels; ISO/IEC 33000 process assessment
Retrospectives, root-cause analysis (fishbone, five whys) and PDCA improvement cycles
Linking improvement to business goals: GQM+Strategies and improvement roadmaps
Change management: adoption, resistance and measuring whether a change worked
Lightweight assessment of agile maturity and team health
Capstone: assess an organisation's process, prioritise improvements and present a plan

schedule.title: Process models and tailoring
schedule.exercise: Compare two processes for a clinic-records project and a payment-switch project, justify the tailoring choices with the home-ground factors, and map the value stream of a feature from idea to release.

tasks.title: Draw the workflow of Scrum, Kanban and a plan-driven model as diagrams, marking feedback loops, artefacts and decision points in each
Advise a start-up and a regulated insurer which process to adopt, using the home-ground factors in the case file, and justify against the rubric
Map a value stream for a feature from request to production, compute flow efficiency from touch and wait times, and propose three waste reductions

schedule.title: Why estimates fail, and parametric estimation
schedule.exercise: Estimate a mobile-money feature set with function points and COCOMO II, then compare with a Delphi round of three estimators and explain the spread.

tasks.title: Compute effort, duration and team size from COCOMO II for a 40 KLOC project with given cost drivers, and plot effort against size
Run a planning-poker session in a case study with biased estimators, and note where anchoring distorts the result and how to correct it
Build a PERT network of 12 activities with three-point estimates, compute expected durations, the critical path and its standard deviation

schedule.title: Uncertainty, simulation and release planning
schedule.exercise: Run a Monte Carlo simulation of a 12-task schedule to give a 50 and 85 percent confidence date, and forecast a release from a team's throughput history.

tasks.title: Run 10,000 Monte Carlo trials on a task network with triangular durations and read the dates for 50, 80 and 95 percent confidence
Forecast the completion of a backlog of 60 items from 12 weeks of throughput data using resampling and show the distribution of finish weeks
Level resources across two projects in a Gantt chart so that a shared team of five is never overbooked, and show the slip in each project

schedule.title: Risk identification and decision analysis
schedule.exercise: Run a pre-mortem on a national ID app rollout, rank the ten risks by exposure, and choose between mitigating and transferring the top two with an expected-value calculation.

tasks.title: Fill a probability-impact matrix for ten risks of a hospital information system project and rank the risks by exposure
Compute expected monetary value on a decision tree for building, buying or outsourcing a module, with probabilities, and find the break-even probability
Manage risks across a six-month branching project case, choosing responses and reserves each month, and see the outcomes scored against the rubric

schedule.title: Measurement and the goal-question-metric approach
schedule.exercise: Derive a metric set from a goal for reducing production defects, define each metric operationally, and read a cumulative flow diagram for a team that has too much work in progress.

tasks.title: Build a goal-question-metric tree for the goal of faster, safer releases, with three questions and two defined metrics per question
Compute defect density, defect escape rate and defect removal efficiency across 5 modules from the data, and rank the modules by risk
Plot a cumulative flow diagram from daily board counts, find the bottleneck stage, and compute average lead time by Little's law

schedule.title: Earned value, delivery metrics and control
schedule.exercise: Compute earned-value indices and the estimate at completion at month 6 of a project, and explain how a team could game velocity and what to measure instead.

tasks.title: Compute PV, EV, AC, CPI, SPI and the estimate at completion for a project at three reporting dates and chart the trend
Compute deployment frequency, lead time, change failure rate and time to restore from a deployment log, and classify the team's performance level
Handle a case where a manager sets a velocity target and the team inflates points, then redesign the measures and justify them against the rubric

schedule.title: Continuous integration and release strategies
schedule.exercise: Design a pipeline for a mobile banking backend with build, test, security scan, staging and canary release, and explain which stage catches which class of failure.

tasks.title: Draw a CI/CD pipeline as a diagram with stages, gates, automated tests and rollback paths for a web service and its mobile client
Roll out a new version to a load-balanced pool as a canary, watch error rates, and roll back when the threshold is exceeded
Define a repeatable environment with a Dockerfile and configuration files, rebuild it on a clean machine, and show that two builds match

schedule.title: Versioning, reliability and incidents
schedule.exercise: Set service-level objectives and an error budget for a payment API, and write a blameless post-incident review for a failed release.

tasks.title: Compute availability, error budget remaining and burn rate from a month of request logs for a 99.9 percent objective
Plan a release of a mobile app update for users on slow networks and old devices, choosing staging, versions and rollback against the rubric
Lead an incident response in a branching scenario, gather evidence, decide on rollback timing and write the post-incident review

schedule.title: Teams, architecture and communication
schedule.exercise: Redraw the team structure of a platform to match its architecture, and set communication practices for a team spanning Accra, Nairobi and Lagos.

tasks.title: Compare a given module architecture with the team structure, mark the mismatches, and redraw the teams to cut cross-team dependencies
Run a distributed team across three time zones in a case study, choosing meeting times and documentation, and handle a missed handover
Negotiate a vendor contract for an outsourced module in a case file, choosing price model, acceptance criteria and exit terms against the rubric

schedule.title: People, culture and leadership
schedule.exercise: Plan how to hire, onboard and retain five developers for a growing team in an African tech hub, and prepare a feedback conversation about a missed deadline.

tasks.title: Handle a conflict between two senior developers over code review in a case study, choosing responses and seeing how team safety changes
Build a hiring and retention plan for a team that loses developers to overseas remote jobs, weighing salary, growth and mentoring in the case file
Design a code review policy as a flow diagram with roles, turnaround targets and escalation, and justify it against delivery data

schedule.title: Scaling, governance and failure analysis
schedule.exercise: Compare scaling frameworks for a ministry's twelve-team programme, choose a contract type for a government system, and write a recovery plan for a project that is a year late.

tasks.title: Draw a portfolio of three products with dependencies and a quarterly planning cycle for 8 teams, marking where the coordination points sit
Choose fixed-price, time-and-materials or outcome-based for a public e-service procurement in a case file, and defend it against the rubric
Recover a failing project in a branching case: reset scope, replan with new estimates, brief the sponsor and see how trust and delivery respond

schedule.title: Process assessment and improvement cycles
schedule.exercise: Assess a small company's process against CMMI-style practice areas, run a root-cause analysis on late releases, and link an improvement to a business goal.

tasks.title: Score a case-file organisation's practices against maturity-model criteria with evidence for each rating, and list the weakest areas
Draw a fishbone diagram for recurring late releases and apply five whys to the three most likely causes, ending in testable actions
Build an improvement roadmap as a Gantt chart with goals, metrics, owners and checkpoints for three improvement initiatives over a year

schedule.title: Change management and capstone
schedule.exercise: Present a process assessment and improvement plan for a software organisation, with measures to show whether the change worked and how resistance will be handled.

tasks.title: Introduce a new review practice in a case study, deal with resistance, and measure adoption and outcomes across three quarters
Assess team health survey results over six sprints with a control chart, and decide which changes are signal and which are noise
Complete the capstone case: assess an organisation, rank improvements by value and effort, and present the plan against the rubric
